Building on the FOMC’s strong-growth, tight-labor-market, and near-2% inflation assessment, the Beige Book references point to broad-based momentum across Districts. Reports from Dallas, Philadelphia, St. Louis, and Kansas City indicate continued expansion; Dallas notes job growth and rising consumer spending, with construction-related hiring strength, while St. Louis describes ongoing manufacturing activity. These anecdotes align with supportive credit conditions from mid-2018 SLOOS (easier C&I standards and narrower spreads, especially among foreign banks), reinforcing a constructive near-term outlook. Some sectoral tightness (e.g., construction labor) remains, but overall conditions tilt positive.

Net effect: With Beige Book corroboration of robust activity and hiring alongside easier bank credit, I nudge the tone modestly higher, still short of exuberant.
